title: Runtime proxy to translate legacy function calls to new tool-calling surface
creator: Marco Silva
description: Provide a lightweight runtime-side proxy that accepts legacy 'functions' invocation payloads and reliably translates them to Redwood's new tool-calling schema (and back) with minimal overhead. The proxy must preserve streaming semantics, structured outputs, and error semantics so existing customers can migrate without changing SDKs immediately.
background: We have multiple customers using legacy function-calling (pre-tool schema) and a growing set of features built around the OpenAI-style 'tools' surface (name/description/json_schema). Past tickets (ENG-5801, ENG-7821) explored adapters and naming normalization, but customers are still blocked by: 1) mismatch in argument encoding and response envelopes, 2) streaming differences when tools emit intermediate events, and 3) breaking changes in field names for nested structured outputs.
proposed_solution: Build a runtime proxy component inside the request router that: (a) detects legacy function invocation signatures via a compatibility header or payload heuristics, (b) maps legacy function names and positional arguments to canonical tool names and JSON schemas using a configurable mapping table, (c) translates streaming chunks so tool events and generated tokens arrive in the original expected shape, (d) wraps/unwraps structured outputs preserving validation errors, and (e) emits metrics tagging requests as 'legacy-proxied' for cost and latency analysis. Provide a feature flag 'legacy_proxy_v2' and a per-customer mapping config in the control plane.
milestones: M1: Design + config schema (2025-02-24) - mapping format, heuristics, feature-flag behavior
M2: Prototype proxy router + basic name mapping (2025-03-03) - non-streaming smoke tests
M3: Streaming compatibility + structured output round-trip tests (2025-03-09)
M4: Perf tuning and canary deploy (2025-03-12)
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Requests using legacy payloads succeed with identical success/failure semantics when proxied
AC2: End-to-end streaming appears identical to callers using legacy SDKs (no token reordering or dropped events)
AC3: Added latency overhead of proxy under median load < 2ms and p95 < 10ms
AC4: Mapping table supports name aliases and argument position -> named param mapping
AC5: Observability: requests tagged and visible in Console with cost/latency breakdowns
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Streaming translation may cause tokenization boundary differences -> Mitigation: build end-to-end conformance tests using recorded client streams
Risk: Mapping rules provide ambiguous name collisions -> Mitigation: warn-and-fail for ambiguous mappings and provide dry-run mode
Risk: Performance regression under high QPS -> Mitigation: optimize hot path in C++ runtime and fallback to direct path for supported customers
testing_plan: Unit tests for mapping logic, fuzz tests for argument encoding, stream replay conformance harness using recorded sessions, and non-regression e2e tests with a staging customer. Add a lightweight chaos test that injects partial chunks to ensure graceful degradation.
rollout_plan: 1) Deploy behind feature flag; 2) Internal canary with QA and platform teams; 3) Pilot with 2 customers with mappings configured; 4) Monitor p95 latency and error rates for 72 hours; 5) Gradual ramp and announce opt-in deprecation timeline for legacy surface.
migration_notes: Provide mapping CLI to generate mapping table from customer SDK calls, recommend customers enable 'legacy_proxy_v2' for a week before switching SDK, and include troubleshooting steps for schema mismatches.
